name: Temporary CSAM Derogation Regulation
impact_assessment: None (Commission judged an IA not appropriate)
evidence_rating: thin: Commission reports say data too incomplete to assess effectiveness or proportionality; no independent study
summary: This temporary law lets messaging services keep voluntarily scanning for child sexual abuse material despite EU privacy rules. Two Commission reports (2023, 2025) say national and platform data are too incomplete to measure its effect reliably, although thousands of children were identified and millions of images removed. Data protection authorities warn safeguards against blanket scanning remain weak.

indicators.objective: No impact assessment (the Commission judged none appropriate given urgency and lack of alternative options) and no LFS indicators; the memorandum says monitoring arrangements are 'not applicable'. The Regulation itself requires provider and Member State statistics (Articles 3 and 8) and Commission implementation reports (Article 9)
Continue voluntary detection and reporting of online child sexual abuse
indicators.indicator: Reports of detected CSA; children identified; offenders convicted
indicators.evidence: Member State data incomplete and fragmented; Commission says a comprehensive and reliable overview of reports, children identified and convictions is not possible. Available data show thousands of children identified and millions of images/videos removed.

indicators.indicator: Error ratios (false positives) of detection technologies
indicators.evidence: Providers report aggregate error ratios using different methods: e.g. Google 1.14% (2023) and 0.54% (2024) of hash-matched flags not confirmed on human review; Meta 0.32% and 0.12% of actioned items restored; Microsoft could not calculate. Not comparable.

indicators.indicator: Balance between child protection and users' privacy
indicators.evidence: Commission: available data insufficient for a definitive answer, though no indications that the derogation is not proportionate; providers gave no information on data protection impact assessments. EDPS (2026) calls for safeguards against general and indiscriminate scanning.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 (temporary derogation from the ePrivacy Directive to combat online child sexual abuse), COM(2023) 797
literature.title: Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 (temporary derogation from the ePrivacy Directive to combat online child sexual abuse)
literature.method: implementation report (provider and Member State statistics)
literature.outcomes: reports; children identified; error rates; data quality
literature.headline: Member States reported for differing periods so EU-level totals of reports and identified child victims could not be calculated; large disparities between NCMEC and national figures
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's first report found national data too patchy to say how many abuse reports or rescued children the voluntary scanning produced.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Second report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/1232, COM(2025) 740
literature.title: Second report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/1232
literature.method: implementation report (provider and Member State statistics 2023-2024)
literature.headline: Data still incomplete and not comparable; providers did not use the mandated reporting form; false-positive ratios reported between 0% and 1.14% with inconsistent methods; data insufficient to answer the proportionality question definitively, but thousands of children identified and millions of items removed
literature.summary_plain: The second Commission report still cannot measure the law's effect reliably, but concludes voluntary scanning helps identify thousands of abused children; error rates reported by platforms are low but calculated inconsistently.

literature.citation: European Data Protection Supervisor (2026), Opinion 7/2026 on the Proposal for a Regulation extending the application of Regulation (EU) 2021/1232, EDPS Opinion, 16 February 2026
literature.title: Opinion 7/2026 on the Proposal for a Regulation extending the application of Regulation (EU) 2021/1232
literature.headline: Recognises child protection as general-interest objective, but says the extension is the time to address key shortcomings of the interim regime and to ensure effective safeguards against general and indiscriminate scanning
literature.summary_plain: The EU's data protection watchdog accepts the aim but says the temporary scanning rules still lack safeguards against blanket monitoring of private messages.

literature.authors: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)
literature.title: European Union CyberTipline Data Snapshot (2020 vs 2021) and updates on the ePrivacy Directive
literature.method: before/after descriptive comparison of CyberTipline reports resolving to EU countries around the Dec 2020 ePrivacy (EECC) change and the Aug 2021 interim derogation
literature.outcomes: number of CSAM reports and files referred to EU countries
literature.headline: EU-related CyberTipline reports fell 47% (1,046,350 to 555,831) and files 58% between 2020 and 2021, while global reports rose 35%; NCMEC reported a 58% drop in the 18 weeks after 21 Dec 2020, before the derogation applied.
literature.summary_plain: When the legal basis for scanning private messages lapsed in late 2020, reports of child abuse material linked to the EU fell sharply, which advocates cite as evidence of what the temporary derogation preserves.
literature.quality: Simple before/after, confounded (e.g. Meta stopped Messenger scanning in the EU for most of 2021); mostly measures the gap before the Regulation applied, i.e. the counterfactual
literature.interested_party: Campaigning NGO (advocated adoption of the derogation)
literature.citation: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) (2022), European Union CyberTipline Data Snapshot (2020 vs 2021) and updates on the ePrivacy Directive, NCMEC 'Child Safety First' web page

literature.title: Processing under EU Regulation 2021/1232 (EU CSAM Derogation report 2025, covering 2024)
literature.method: provider transparency report required by Art. 3(1)(g)(vii): counts of detections, appeals and reversals for hash-matching on Messenger and Instagram Direct
literature.outcomes: CSAM detections, user appeals, error (overturn) rate
literature.headline: Meta actioned about 1.5 million pieces of CSAM media in EU-related private message threads in 2024; about 76.9 thousand were appealed and 1.8 thousand restored, an overturn rate of 0.12%.
literature.summary_plain: Meta says its automatic matching of known abuse images in private messages involving EU users flagged about 1.5 million items in 2024, and only about one in a thousand was later found to be a mistake.
literature.quality: Self-reported by a firm subject to the act, not audited; overturn rate understates errors (only appealed cases)
literature.citation: Meta Platforms Ireland Ltd (2025), Processing under EU Regulation 2021/1232 (EU CSAM Derogation report 2025, covering 2024), Meta Transparency Center

literature.title: Submission to the European Commission's post-adoption consultation on Combating online child sexual abuse - amending temporary derogation from certain provisions of Directive 2002/58/EC
literature.method: structured critique of the Commission's 2023 implementation report and provider transparency data (re-analysis of reported error rates)
literature.outcomes: evidence of necessity/effectiveness, false-positive rates of detection tools
literature.headline: Using the only provider that reported actual error rates under the Regulation, EDRi shows LinkedIn's automated tools flagged 75 items of which only 31 were confirmed as CSAM in 2021, a 59% false-positive rate, versus the 99.9% accuracy cited by the Commission.
literature.summary_plain: A digital-rights network argues that the Commission's own report on the temporary scanning rules contains no solid evidence that scanning private messages has helped protect children, and that the little real data available shows many false alarms.
literature.quality: Secondary analysis of official report data; very small sample for the error-rate figure; written by a campaigning organisation.
literature.interested_party: Campaigning digital-rights NGO network opposed to CSAM scanning of private communications
literature.citation: European Digital Rights (EDRi) (2024), Submission to the European Commission's post-adoption consultation on Combating online child sexual abuse - amending temporary derogation from certain provisions of Directive 2002/58/EC, EDRi
